title: Match result codec for a game stats API
name: Match result codec

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code serializes or deserializes match results (IDs, timestamps, optional fields)? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
A client sends "started_at": "2026-03-01T18:00:00" (no zone suffix). What does submit return?
choices: 201, with the time interpreted as UTC
201, with the time interpreted in the server's local zone

questions.prompt: Why does encodeMatchResult call m.playerId.toString() instead of placing the bigint directly in the returned object?
choices: JSON.stringify throws a TypeError on bigint values, and a JSON number would also lose precision above 2^53 in most clients
toString() is needed to strip leading zeros
Without it the ID would be serialized as an object with a value field
It is only a style choice; JSON.stringify handles bigint natively
